sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesian tech names (CENT, ALAB) are decoupling from US semis, driven by local retail liquidity and index inclusion flows, not earnings revisions.
US AI infrastructure demand continues to concentrate in capital equipment (KLAC) and custom silicon (MRVL), making these the most durable beneficiaries of hyperscaler capex.
Storage and optical components (SNDK, COHR) are re-rating on supply tightness and 1.6T transceiver adoption, a structural cycle independent of AI model monetization.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech exposure via CENT and ALAB momentum, but hedge with US semis (KLAC, MRVL) as AI capex flows remain the core driver. Expect rotation into storage (SNDK) and networking (NBIS) names; trim TOSK after its spike. Position for Q2 earnings beats in US names, while ID names benefit from domestic liquidity, not fundamentals.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: Indonesian financials are decoupling from US peers due to domestic rate stability and loan growth, making local catalysts—mergers, digital banking pivots, and niche financing—the primary alpha source.
Small-cap financials like POLA, BMAS, and BSIM are seeing outsized moves on thin liquidity, so position sizing and exit discipline matter more than sector beta.
Regulatory tailwinds for sharia-compliant financing and micro-lending are lifting second-tier banks, but sustainability depends on asset quality and funding costs, not just price action.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian financials on idiosyncratic catalysts, not beta: POLA, BMAS, BSIM, and ABDA are pricing in deal-driven or earnings re-ratings that can persist for weeks. US financial weakness is a headwind, but local momentum and NORMAL signal favor holding winners. Add on dips in BSIM and ABDA; avoid chasing LIFE and WIDI without fundamental confirmation.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Coal exporters with integrated logistics and captive power are structurally advantaged as global supply constraints and Indonesian domestic market obligations keep margins sticky.
State-owned miners (PTBA) benefit from policy-driven volume targets and infrastructure spending, offering defensive cash flows amid commodity price volatility.
Nickel and downstream processing names (AADI) ride the EV battery supply chain reshoring wave, with Indonesia's ore export ban cementing local value-add as a durable growth driver.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into coal names with captive power or export logistics (FPNI, DOID, BUMI) as ID outperformance persists despite weak US sentiment; momentum is broad but not euphoric, so rotate from laggards into leaders on pullbacks. Favor PTBA for state-backed volume upside and AADI for nickel-linked optionality, but trim any position if IDX energy reverses below its 20-day.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: AI datacenter load growth is a durable, multi-year driver for US IPPs and utilities, rewarding merchant power exposure over pure renewables.
Indonesia's energy transition hinges on JETP financing and grid upgrades, but execution risk keeps local climate-tech names speculative versus US peers.
Power price volatility and nuclear/SMR optionality (CEG) are re-rating catalysts that separate winners from laggards in this sector.
sectors.ai: Buy the US power-demand complex (NRG, CEG, VST) on AI/DC load visibility; Indonesia's lagging +0.40% offers entry into LAPD/PLUG only on policy catalysts—rotate toward US-listed yieldcos and avoid local names until tariff clarity.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rural consumption recovery and government cash transfers are structurally lifting volume growth for mass-market FMCG players, favoring those with deep Java distribution networks.
Premiumization and health-conscious product shifts (functional foods, personal care) are creating durable margin expansion for brands that successfully innovate packaging and formulations.
E-commerce and quick-commerce penetration in tier-2/3 cities is reshaping FMCG go-to-market, giving agile local players a structural cost and speed advantage over legacy incumbents.
sectors.ai: Buy dips in FMCG small/mid caps with confirmed volume breakouts (MSJA, FOLK, KING) as domestic demand holds firm despite US softness; rotate out of laggards lacking earnings catalysts. Target names with strong rural distribution and digital channel growth, as sector consolidation and premiumization sustain momentum through 2H25.
